title: **db-quality: `audit --db-url` reports BDB330
notes: on a CHECK-constrained column (filed 2026-11-08 from compratuentrada).**
The live schema is typed with `kysely-codegen`, which maps a `varchar` to
always drifts; a `disable` entry matches the whole code (`isDisabled`
compares `entry.code` only), and the README's "constrain the column (a
CHECK ...)" and "accept the finding in the baseline" advice is wrong for
still reports BDB330". Next step: read a single-column `IN`/`= ANY` CHECK
as a literal union in type drift, or let a `disable` entry name a
`table.column` subject, and fix the two README claims.
result: A disable entry on a BDB330/ code accepts a subject (table or table.column) and drops only that finding; a subject on any other code is a ConfigError. README now says a CHECK does not narrow kysely-codegen's type and that audit findings never reach the baseline; CHANGELOG Unreleased entry added.
evidence: pnpm test --no-file-parallelism in packages/db-quality: 530 passed; new cases in isDisabled, disableEntriesFrom and runKyselyTypeDrift tests; eslint, type-check, root knip/dupes/oxlint green.
